the relationship between insulin and brain activation in response to food cues in normal weight and obese adolescents.
the role of insulin and hippocampus activation in obesity and the development of obesity‐related metabolic disorders in adolescents.
the question of how the brain regulates food intake.

the hippocampal activity after stimulation with high caloric food images is associated with insulin resistance, which is an important factor for the development of abdominal obesity.
insulin signaling pathways may be a factor that influences the hippocampus and its control of eating behavior in adolescents.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hippocampus may be involved in the regulation of eating behavior in adolescents.
the insulin‐hippocampus axis may play a role in the pathophysiology of abdominal obesity.
the insulin‐dependent activation of the hippocampal system in response to food cues is a risk factor for obesity, and may be an indicator for a future development towards obesity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hippocampus is an important brain structure in obesity, and it may play a role in the regulation of food intake.
the hippocampal activity in response to food cues may play a key role in the development of obesity, especially in adolescents.
insulin signaling pathways in hippocampal neurons may play a crucial role in the central regulation and control of eating behavior in obese adolescents.
